title: She Won the World Cup Last Year. On Sunday, Harmanpreet Leads India Against Pakistan at Edgbaston.
excerpt: India begin their Women's T20 World Cup campaign against arch-rivals Pakistan in Birmingham, where the UK's Indian diaspora will turn the stands into a second home
body:
Harmanpreet Kaur led India to the ODI World Cup title last October. On Sunday, she will walk out at Edgbaston for the most charged fixture in women's cricket: India against Pakistan, in the opening match of both teams' T20 World Cup campaign.

The match starts at 2:30 PM local time in Birmingham — that is 7:00 PM IST and 6:30 AM on the US West Coast — and it promises to be the most-watched contest of the group stage.

A Champion Under Pressure

India arrive in England as defending 50-over world champions but in underwhelming T20I form. They lost the bilateral series against South Africa 4-1 in May and then fell to England 2-1 in the build-up to the tournament. In the warm-up matches, Harmanpreet's squad beat West Indies by 26 runs but then lost to the hosts by five runs in Cardiff.

But India's captain has thrived in exactly these conditions before. With over 4,075 T20I runs, one century, and 17 half-centuries, Harmanpreet remains the most dangerous middle-order batter in the women's game. She has scored 291 runs in 10 T20Is this year — the most by any Indian woman.

Nasser Hussain, the former England captain, has backed Smriti Mandhana to deliver on the big stage. "Come Sunday, I think Smriti Mandhana will absolutely raise her level," Hussain said. "If she bats 20 overs, she will either have a hundred or be pretty close to one."

Pakistan's Bowling Card

!World Cup — Photo: Wikimedia Commons

Pakistan's campaign hinges on the fitness of captain Fatima Sana, who suffered a right knee injury during practice. The all-rounder has taken 48 T20I wickets and scored 715 runs at a strike rate of nearly 140. If she plays, Pakistan have a genuine match-winner who can change the game with both bat and ball.

Opening batter Muneeba Ali will be tasked with giving Pakistan early momentum, while Tuba Hassan's off-spin could prove crucial on an Edgbaston surface that has traditionally offered modest run rates — the average women's T20I run rate here over the past four years sits at 6.55.

India's probable XI features Shafali Verma and Mandhana opening, Jemimah Rodrigues at three, Harmanpreet at four, and Richa Ghosh behind the stumps. Ghosh's form is the most encouraging sign — she smashed 68 off 36 balls in the warm-up loss to England, with nine fours and two sixes, and looks ready for the tournament.

The Group and What's at Stake

India are in the tougher of the two groups, alongside Australia, South Africa, Pakistan, Bangladesh, and the Netherlands. Every game matters: India play the Netherlands on June 17 in Leeds, South Africa on June 21 in Manchester, Bangladesh on June 25, and Australia on June 28 at Lord's.

In the other group, hosts England are the favourites after demolishing Sri Lanka by 87 runs in the tournament opener at Edgbaston on Thursday. Scotland beat Ireland and West Indies pipped New Zealand by a single run in Saturday's action.

Where to Watch

NRIs in the UK have the rare chance to watch India play a World Cup on home soil. Edgbaston is a 10-minute walk from Birmingham New Street station, and the city's massive South Asian community means the atmosphere will feel like a subcontinent derby.

For NRIs in North America, the match starts at 9:30 AM Eastern and 6:30 AM Pacific. JioHotstar has the live streaming rights in India, while Willow TV covers the US market. In the UK, Sky Sports has the broadcast rights.

The last time India and Pakistan met in a T20 World Cup, over 100 million viewers tuned in. On Sunday, with a trophy defence on the line and the diaspora filling Edgbaston's stands, it could be louder than ever.
